subject: Request: approval for amended uptime target & one-time remedy (Quantum Health)
messages:
From: Caroline Meyers <caroline@quantumhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@quantumhealth.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA questions — uptime target and remedies

Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement ran the numbers and we have two items blocking legal sign-off: the uptime target in Section 5 and the cumulative service credit cap in Section 7. Our security and ops teams are asking that we either reduce the uptime target to 99.5% for the first 12 months or accept a one-time remediation credit and remove recurring monthly SLA credits.

We appreciate Redwood's standard 99.9% target, but given our expected production load and heavy peak windows, the lower target + a one-time credit makes our board comfortable. Can you confirm whether Redwood can agree to: 1) set the uptime target to 99.5% for the initial 12-month term; and 2) replace recurring monthly service credits with a capped one-time credit (we proposed $60k) that would be the sole remedy?

Attached is a short note from our ops team with the rationale (Quantum-Requested-Remedy-Changes.pdf). Procurement is on a tight timetable — they asked for a decision in 48 hours.

Best,
Caroline
Caroline Meyers
Head of Procurement, Quantum Health

---
Attachment: Quantum-Requested-Remedy-Changes.pdf (summary; 2 pages)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Meyers <caroline@quantumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions — uptime target and remedies

Caroline — thanks for the clear ask and the note. Marissa and I ran the numbers and modeled risk/ cost across expected Q1 traffic. Quick summary of options we can present to Legal: 

Option A (preferred for Redwood): keep 99.9% uptime, keep standard monthly credits, but increase the cumulative cap from 6 months to 9 months for the first year only.

Option B (compromise): accept 99.5% uptime for the first 12 months + one-time remediation credit of $50k paid if uptime drops below the agreed threshold. No ongoing monthly credits during that period.

Option C (customer ask): 99.5% uptime + one-time $60k credit (no recurring credits) — this reduces Redwood's recurring exposure but increases one-time liability.

Operational note: Option B limits our long-term exposure while acknowledging their board's ask; Option C is feasible but requires exec sign-off due to credit size and precedent risk. I included a basic impact calc in SLA-Impact-Calc.xlsx.

Marissa — can you confirm the deal economics and whether a one-time $60k concession still meets our margin guardrails? Vivek — will need a quick seat at the table on any approval here.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: SLA-Impact-Calc.xlsx (model; shows expected monthly token spend vs credit exposure)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Legal Team (redacted) <legal@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions — uptime target and remedies

Team — quick escalation. I reviewed the numbers. One-time $60k is on the high side from a precedent perspective but acceptable if we make two non-negotiable guardrails: 1) one-time credit is the exclusive remedy for uptime failures during the first 12 months (explicitly waive future monthly credits for incidents in that period), and 2) add a rollback clause so that starting in month 13 we revert to standard 99.9% uptime and standard SLA credit mechanics.

If Legal can get language that (a) caps total liability to the $60k credit during Year 1, and (b) includes clear thresholds for what constitutes an SLA event and how measurements are calculated, I will sign off. Marissa — will this approval require any pricing concession beyond the $60k? If so, escalate.

Also loop in Finance for the accounting treatment of a $60k one-time credit (needs to be logged as contra-revenue). Legal — please prioritize a redline for the remedy section with the two guardrails above. Caroline — assuming the above, can we get a quick confirmation you will accept the one-time credit as exclusive remedy for Year 1?

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Global Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Legal Team (redacted) <legal@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions — uptime target and remedies

Thanks for the clear framing. I approve Option C (one-time $60k credit + 99.5% for 12 months) on the following conditions: 

- Legal to produce a firm redline that limits Year 1 remedy liability to a single $60k credit and explicitly waives monthly credits for incidents during the first 12 months.
- Add measurement clarity: use Redwood's per-route availability logging with agreed sampling windows; provide daily uptime reports and a single-point escalation for any disputed incident measurement.
- Require procurement to sign a mutual rollback clause that reverts SLA to 99.9% and standard crediting mechanics starting month 13 automatically.
- Pricing: no additional discount beyond the $60k credit; Marissa, confirm this does not alter revenue recognition thresholds.
- One-time credit to be issued as a contra-revenue line item and processed within 30 days after a validated incident for which the credit is payable. Finance & Legal to confirm mechanics.

Once Legal posts the redline, Jonas/Marissa you have my authorization to accept the amended terms and finalize the DocuSign. Vivek — flag me if any stakeholder pushes materially beyond these conditions.

Laura Bennett
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference
